text: Every terraform apply writes a terraform.tfstate file mapping your config to the real resources it created. With no backend block configured, that file lives on disk, on whoever's laptop ran the command — fine for a solo learning project, but it quietly breaks down the moment a second person needs to work against the same real infrastructure.

With no backend block anywhere in the configuration, Terraform defaults to the local backend: terraform.tfstate lands in the current working directory on disk. It's a JSON record of every resource ID and attribute Terraform knows about for each block in your config, and that record is exactly how plan can tell what already exists instead of guessing and risking a duplicate.

Local state fails a team three distinct ways. A teammate's fresh checkout has no copy of your state file at all, so their plan honestly wants to create everything from scratch against infrastructure that already exists. Two people applying within the same few minutes can overwrite or corrupt the same file, since local state has no locking mechanism to stop them. And the state file routinely holds database passwords, storage keys, and connection strings in plain text, completely unencrypted, whether or not you marked those values sensitive in your config.

That last point is exactly why terraform.tfstate never belongs in a git repository, even a private one — committing it pushes every secret it holds into your commit history, essentially permanently and readable by anyone with repo access. Every real Terraform project's .gitignore excludes *.tfstate, *.tfstate.*, and the .terraform/ provider cache directory from version control entirely.

Fixing both problems at once — no shared source of truth for the team, and secrets sitting unencrypted on a laptop — means getting state off any one machine entirely and into one durable, shared location instead: a remote backend. Lesson 10 configures a real azurerm backend against an Azure Storage Account and a real s3 backend against an AWS S3 bucket, side by side.
